headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 22 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend.
Mostly dry and seasonable conditions continue through the weekend.
Seasonable and mainly dry weather will continue through at least the first half of next week.

ALY.excerpt: ) Mainly dry weather will continue through this weekend into early next week with the only chance for some light showers on Thu night, especially for areas north and west of Albany.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure continues to dominate the weather into next week. Expect dry conditions and no significant weather impacts.

BUF.excerpt:
)Record warmth possible on Thursday.
)A brief shot of light rain Thursday night. Dry weather then resumes and lasts through the weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
Spotty minor tidal flooding expected with Thursday morning's high tide.
Patchy fog possible tomorrow morning. Otherwise, no other significant weather concerns over the next several days.

CTP.excerpt:
) Rain-free and mild conditions through the end of October
) Fire weather concerns increasing by Friday

RLX.excerpt: ) Dry and slightly above seasonable weather dominates into the weekend. Rain chances returns to the forecast for the beginning of November.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:16}} to {{t:55}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 31).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Wednesday 2:40 PM: "Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans warmer than normal and slightly wetter than normal. Wet and mild often means rain below the summits.
